about: OSSIE-012a fixture corpus: what each file is and what each entry point does with it. Synthetic data only. tests/ossie_corpus.py reads it; tests/test_ossie_corpus.py checks it; tools/ossie_upgrade_diff.py compares two converters over it. findings are recorded, not fixed.

files.what: Ossie 0.2: one dataset, one field (richness 1).
Ossie 0.2: two datasets, a relationship and a model metric in SQL (richness 2).
Ossie 0.2: dataset metrics, AI context, unique keys, a time dimension and several dialects (richness 3).
Ossie 0.2 exported from tmsl/02_rich.bim: a POWER_BI section with a role, hierarchy, calculation group, perspective and culture (richness 4).
findings: Roles come back Fully preserved on Import: the role reaches the model from the POWER_BI extension, so the fidelity report of Ossie to TMSL classes it Fully preserved with no security warning, although in the file only Power BI could read it.

files.what: The minimal model written as JSON.
A Fabric Semantic View: datasets without fields, a relationship, DAX on every metric.
findings: A Semantic View converted to TMDL drops its relationships: a view has no fields, so the converter finds no column for either end and skips each relationship, reported as lost (relationship 'orders_customers').

files.what: TMSL: one Direct Lake table with a measure.
TMSL: a role, a hierarchy, a calculation group, a perspective, a culture and a multi-line measure.
notes: Every Power BI-only object exports Preserved through extensions and the round trip is the same.

files.what: TMDL folder of tmsl/02_rich.bim.
TMDL folder with an object kind KratosForge can't read (calendar).
notes: The calendar is reported by the TMDL reader as not understood and left out; nothing raises.
